definition: GPT-6.1 Sol is OpenAI's model released at DevDay 2026, one week after GPT-6 Sol. It's tuned for agentic coding, computer use, and professional work — and OpenAI says it delivers intelligence close to its flagship GPT-6 Astra at one-fifth of Astra's input and output token prices: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output, versus Astra's $10 and $50. It's the model most developers will actually afford to leave running for hours. An Ultrafast speed option was expected soon after launch. (Sol is the efficiency play; GPT-6.1 Astra, a flagship upgrade, was cancelled the day before DevDay after failing safety testing.)

edges.label: the closed efficiency play
edges.note: Like DeepSeek, Sol is about doing more per dollar — but closed-source and tuned for agents.

edges.label: exists to tame
edges.note: An always-on agent burns tokens for hours; a 5x price cut is what makes that survivable.

edges.label: priced per
edges.note: The headline numbers — $2 in, $10 out per million — are the economics of the agentic era.

example.body: A small company runs a coding agent overnight, burning through 20 million input tokens. On Astra at standard pricing that's $200 of input tokens; on GPT-6.1 Sol it's $40 — for what OpenAI says is near-flagship quality. That's the arithmetic behind leaving agents on: the difference between a demo you can afford and one you can't.
example.title: The agent that pays for itself

footnotes.body: Per OpenAI's announcement: $2 per million input tokens, $10 per million output; cached input at $0.10 per million, which OpenAI describes as 95% below standard input pricing and 50% below GPT-6 Sol's cached input price. Available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users, and via the API as gpt-6.1-sol; not yet in Chat at launch.
footnotes.label: Pricing and availability

footnotes.body: Per CNBC's live coverage, OpenAI pulled its planned GPT-6.1 Astra launch on September 28 — the day before DevDay — because the model did not meet its safety standards. The cancelled flagship is worth remembering next to the efficient model's launch: capability and safety are negotiated separately.
footnotes.label: The cancelled flagship

name: GPT-6.1 Sol
tagline: OpenAI's efficient workhorse: near-flagship smarts for agentic coding at one-fifth the price.
whyItMatters: Flagship models get the headlines; the efficient model decides what actually gets built. When an always-on agent burns tokens for hours, a 5x price cut is the difference between a demo and a product. This is the cost curve that makes dots and the Agents API economically real.
